blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the very top, cloud strategy is no longer about which provider to use. It is about what kind of company the cloud lets you become. The big choices — single cloud, multi-cloud, hybrid with on-premise — each shape the company differently. Each has its own cost profile, its own dependency, its own freedom and its own ceiling.

Had we committed to one provider three years ago without thinking about lock-in, we would now be negotiating from a weaker position than we actually are. The fact that we deliberately kept a second provider alive — small, but genuinely alive — is the reason we have leverage today.

Senior cloud strategy has one deep question underneath the technical ones: how much of our destiny do we want to hand to a single external company, and how much are we willing to pay to keep more of it in our own hands? The answer is rarely 'as much as possible' in either direction. It is almost always a careful, deliberate balance — and that balance is a strategic conversation, not a procurement one.

items.q: According to the text, what is cloud strategy at the very top really about?
options: Which provider is cheapest to use
Which procurement team should own the contract
How many servers to keep on-premise
What kind of company the cloud lets you become
items.why: "It is about what kind of company the cloud lets you become" — a escolha é estratégica, não técnica.

items.q: Why does the company have leverage in today's negotiation?
options: It standardised on a single provider early
It deliberately kept a second provider genuinely alive
It renegotiates the contract every year
items.why: "The fact that we deliberately kept a second provider alive… is the reason we have leverage today."

items.q: What does each structural cloud choice have, according to the first paragraph?
options: A guaranteed path to lower spending
Its own cost profile, dependency, freedom and ceiling
The same cost and the same risk
items.why: "Each has its own cost profile, its own dependency, its own freedom and its own ceiling."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Lock-in is a strategic risk, not just a technical detail.
Optionality can be worth paying for.
Choosing a cloud model reshapes the company itself.
Consolidating on a single provider is always the smart, cheapest move.
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto defende manter opção aberta; 'padronizar sempre' contraria a tese de leverage.

items.q: The sentence beginning "Had we committed to one provider three years ago…" suggests that…
options: the provider was never a real risk
the company is regretting keeping a second provider
the past decision to preserve optionality is paying off now
items.why: Inferência: o condicional passado contrafactual mostra que a escolha de manter optionality evitou a posição mais fraca de hoje.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry na sala de renegociação com o fornecedor de nuvem. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making the time. Before we get into pricing, I want to be honest about where we're sitting, because it changes the tone of this conversation.

Three years ago, everyone in my own team was pushing me to standardise entirely on your platform. It would have been cheaper on paper and cleaner to run. And I held the line — we kept a second provider small but genuinely alive. Had I given in back then, I'd be walking in today with almost nothing to trade. I'd be a captive account, and we'd both know it.

So let me be direct. We are not here to threaten anyone. We like your service, and moving would be painful and expensive — I won't pretend otherwise. But 'painful' is a very different word from 'impossible', and that difference is exactly what we've spent three years protecting.

What I'm looking for is a partnership that reflects that reality: better commitment terms from us, in exchange for pricing and portability guarantees from you. If we can land that, you keep the vast majority of our workload for years.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Harry mention keeping a second provider alive?
options: To justify raising the company's cloud budget
To announce he is leaving the provider immediately
To explain why he now has something to trade in the negotiation
To apologise for a mistake his team warned him about
items.why: "Had I given in back then, I'd be walking into this room today with almost nothing to trade."

items.q: What was Harry's own team pushing him to do three years ago?
options: Split the workload across four providers
Standardise entirely on the provider's platform
items.why: "everyone in my own team was pushing me to standardise entirely on your platform."

items.q: How does Harry describe the option of moving away from this provider?
options: Painful and expensive, but not impossible
items.why: "'painful' is a very different word from 'impossible'" — doloroso, mas viável.

items.q: What does Harry mean when he says he would have been "a captive account"?
options: He would have paid nothing for the service
He would have owned the provider's technology
He would have been locked in with no real alternative
He would have had strong negotiating power
items.why: Inferência: captive account = aprisionado ao fornecedor, sem alternativa — o oposto de ter leverage.

items.q: Which best describes Harry's overall stance in the meeting?
options: Aggressive and threatening to walk out
Cooperative but negotiating from genuine strength
items.why: Inferência: ele elogia o serviço e quer parceria, mas deixa claro que tem alternativa real — força sem hostilidade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "By keeping two providers, we avoided lock-in and preserved room to manoeuvre." Lock-in means…
options: being trapped with one supplier with no easy exit
items.why: Lock-in = aprisionamento: ficar preso a um fornecedor sem saída barata.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The second provider is small, but it is exactly what gives us ___ at the table."
items.why: Leverage = alavancagem, poder de barganha na negociação.

items.q: "Every model has its own cost profile." A cost profile is…
options: the shape of how and where the costs fall over time
the name of the finance director
items.why: Cost profile = perfil de custo: como os custos se distribuem e evoluem.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A ___ setup keeps some workloads on-premise and moves the rest to the cloud."
items.why: Hybrid = híbrido: mistura on-premise e nuvem.

items.q: "This is a strategic conversation, not a procurement one." Procurement refers to…
options: the buying and sourcing of goods and services
the long-term direction of the company
items.why: Procurement = compras/aquisição — o processo de contratar fornecedores, distinto da estratégia.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em negociações com fornecedores. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the new cloud contract." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "If negotiations stall, we can always fall back on the second provider." To fall back on means to…
items.why: Fall back on = recorrer a algo como plano B, alternativa de segurança.

items.q: "Several architects pushed back on keeping a second vendor." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to standardise, but nobody followed through on the migration." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "A tiny discount like that won't move the needle on our total cloud spend." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
